card.text: The most volcanically active body in the solar system.

introduction.text: Tides from Jupiter, Europa and Ganymede power Io's hundreds of volcanoes. Fresh lava keeps filling its craters.

normal.title: Global image mosaic
normal.summary: Detail ranges from 1 to 10 km per pixel. Shadows in the photographs remain.

enhanced.title: False-color mosaic
enhanced.summary: Infrared, green and violet ratios color the monochrome detail. Polar color is withheld.

geology.title: Global geologic map
geology.summary: Fourteen interpreted units, such as plains, lava flows, patera floors and mountains, from Voyager and Galileo.

spectral-slope.title: Sulfur-sensitive visible spectral slope
spectral-slope.summary: A visible slope sensitive to sulfur, from 2019 VLT observations. It does not measure how much sulfur there is.

visible-absorption.title: Continuum-relative visible absorption
visible-absorption.summary: A broad 520–660 nm absorption from 2019 VLT observations; which chemical causes it is uncertain.

volcanic-heat.title: Global map of volcanic hot spots
volcanic-heat.summary: 343 hot spots colored by thermal power, up to Juno's 49th orbit. Symbol size marks the power class, not the spot's size.
